shared-chrome.summary: The shared chrome is recognisably the same product but not the same layout: the nav is 10px short, inset 76px a side and uses a pill CTA with a smaller logo, the footer has the wrong link columns (one dead link), wrong layout and wrong ink, and every button is a pill where Figma uses 10-12px rectangles. The biggest problems are two dead links ('How it works' in the nav, /how-it-works in the footer), the footer link inventory, and two AA contrast failures (--sc-text-muted in the footer and Loading text), plus tokens that pages do not use (gutters, section padding, type ramp).
shared-chrome.audit_notes: Chrome style dumps are scratch evidence only (not saved under figma-style/): scratchpad/audit/chrome-nav.json (468:126), chrome-footer.json (479:133), chrome-nav.diff.txt, chrome-footer.diff.txt, nav-home.png, footer-home.png. Nav/footer consistency, button census, section/gutter census and type census were read-only use_figma scans over the 15 page frames.

findings.title: Nav bar is 69px tall, Figma draws 79px
findings.figma: Nav frame 468:126 is 1440x79: padding 20/48/20/48 around a 39px CTA, with a 1px #2b323d bottom stroke inside the frame. All 14 page frames carry an identical Nav (485:125, 483:125, 487:125, 496:125, 506:125 ...), and the first section of every page starts at y=79.
findings.build: header.navbar-header measures 1440x69: .navbar-container height 68px (Navbar.vue:310) plus 1px border-bottom (Navbar.vue:294). tokens.css:66 --nav-height is 68px, which is itself 1px short of the real 69. Every page's content therefore starts 10px higher than in Figma (build y=69 vs Figma y=79), which shows up as a -10px offset in every page's style diff.
findings.evidence: home.blink.dom.json items[0] header h=69. Figma extract 468:126 h=79. use_figma scan of all 15 page frames: every Nav child h=79, pad [20,48,20,48].
findings.fix: Make the header 79px: .navbar-container height 78px (+1px border) or padding 20px + 39px CTA. Set --nav-height: 79px in tokens.css:66; AdminShell, AffiliateShell, anchors.css, LegalPage and DocsArticleView all read the token, so they follow. Land this first: the page tickets' dy figures were measured against a 69px nav.

findings.title: Nav content is inset 124px by a 1240px max-width, Figma runs the bar at 48px gutters
findings.figma: Nav content spans the full 1440 frame: logo (494:124) at x=48, CTA (468:138) right edge at x=1392. Gutter 48px. (The page body uses 96px gutters; only the nav is 48.)
findings.build: Navbar.vue:305-309 .navbar-container max-width 1240px, margin 0 auto, padding 0 24px, so at 1440 the logo is at x=124 and the CTA right edge at x=1316 (76px more inset each side than Figma).
findings.evidence: vp_style_diff --figma chrome-nav.json: SelahCue x +70.0 (figma 88, build 158); Features x +71.5; How it works x +70.6; Pricing x +70.5; Download x +70.2; Sign in x -84.0; Download free x -76.6. dom brand-logo x=124. Slice nav-home.png.
findings.fix: Drop the 1240px max-width cap (or raise it above 1440) and set padding-inline: 48px from 1200px up. The existing tablet/mobile steps (24px/20px) can stay. Result: lockup starts at x=48 and the CTA ends at x=1392 at 1440.

findings.title: Brand lockup: mark renders about 15px instead of 32px (nav) and 19px instead of 28px (footer); gaps, wordmark and alt text differ
findings.figma: Nav lockup 468:128: logo 494:124 32x32 (tight-cropped mark), gap 8, wordmark 19/Bold #eef1f6 with 0 tracking; lockup-to-links gap 40 (468:127). Footer lockup 479:136: logo 494:128 28x28, gap 8, wordmark 18/Bold #eef1f6. Handoff section 7: 32px nav / 28px footer, and the source PNG has ~33% transparent padding so either trim it or size the img up to compensate.
findings.build: Navbar.vue:333-336 img.brand-logo height 24px (a 24x24 box of the untrimmed 1254x1254 PNG whose mark bbox is 760x835, so the visible mark is about 15x16px), brand gap 10 (:326), wordmark 19/700 in #ffffff with -0.01em tracking (:338-343), lockup-to-links gap 44 (:320). Footer.vue:166-177 img.logo 32px untrimmed (visible mark about 19x21px), gap 12, wordmark 20/700 -0.02em in --sc-text. Both img carry alt='SelahCue Logo' inside a link that also contains the visible wordmark, so it is announced twice (handoff section 6: alt 'SelahCue logo' only when alone, aria-hidden next to the wordmark).
findings.evidence: dom: nav img.brand-logo w=24 h=24 x=124; footer img.logo w=32 h=32; footer wordmark fs 20px ls -0.4px. marketing/public/selahcue-logo.png alpha bbox (247,215,1007,1050) of 1254x1254. vp_style_diff: SelahCue colour figma #eef1f6 vs build #ffffff. Slice nav-home.png shows the mark visibly smaller in the build.
findings.fix: Ship a tight-cropped logo (crop to the alpha bbox on a square canvas) or scale the img by 1/0.67 with matching negative margin, so the visible mark is 32px in the nav and 28px in the footer. Gaps 8/8, lockup-to-links 40, footer wordmark 18px with 0 tracking, nav and footer wordmark colour var(--sc-text). Give the img alt='' aria-hidden='true' (the wordmark names the link).

findings.title: Active route is Medium/white in the build, Figma is Semi Bold in text/primary

findings.fix: .nav-item.active { color: var(--sc-text); font-weight: 600; } and keep the hover rule colour-only. Accept the ~1px link shift the Figma frames themselves show (How it works x=305 vs 306 on Features).

findings.title: 'Download free' nav CTA is a 999px pill at weight 600, Figma is a 10px-radius rectangle at weight 700
findings.figma: Btn/Download 468:138 (cloned on all 14 pages): 136x39, radius 10, fill #5b6bd6 (accent/brand), padding 11/18, label Inter Bold 14 white (#ffffff).

findings.title: Nav 'How it works' is a dead link on every page: nothing carries id='how-it-works'
findings.figma: The nav draws 'How it works' as the second link on every page (frame 468:131, x=305). Handoff section 1: 'How it works' is an in-page anchor on Home (Home section 6, node 476:124).
findings.build: Navbar.vue:191 (desktop) and :261 (mobile sheet) render <a href='#how-it-works'>, but no element in the app has that id: HomeView.vue:263-264 <section class='steps-section'> has no id, and grep finds the string only in the navbar, the footer and a comment in router/scroll.ts:13. On Home the click changes the hash and scrolls nowhere; on every other page it only appends #how-it-works to the current URL (the href is not rooted at '/').
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'how-it-works' src: Navbar.vue:191,261; Footer.vue:25; router/scroll.ts:13 (comment). dom: nav-item href '#how-it-works' on features, pricing, download, about, account captures.
findings.fix: Navbar.vue:191 and :261 -> <router-link :to="{ path: '/', hash: '#how-it-works' }" class='nav-item'>. Add id='how-it-works' to HomeView's steps section in the Home ticket (with scroll-margin-top: var(--sc-anchor-offset)), and add 'home' to ANCHORED_ROUTES in router/scroll.ts so the heading clears the sticky bar.

findings.title: Desktop nav links, brand and CTA have no :focus-visible style, they fall back to the browser default ring
findings.figma: Figma draws no focus state; handoff section 5: focus-visible is a 2px accent/brand ring with a 2px offset, and section 6: every button/link needs that visible ring.
findings.build: Navbar.vue declares :focus-visible only for .mobile-toggle and .sheet-close (:458-462) and .mobile-link/.sheet-cta (:571, :622). .brand, .nav-item, .signin-btn, .signout-btn and .download-cta have no rule, so they show the UA default (Footer links and UiButton do use the 2px --sc-primary ring). main.css has no global a:focus-visible either.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'focus-visible' Navbar.vue: lines 458, 459, 571, 622 only; main.css: none; Footer.vue:227-233 has the 2px --sc-primary / 2px offset recipe.
findings.fix: Add a global default in main.css (a:focus-visible, button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--sc-primary); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 6px }) so no component can forget it, and keep the existing component overrides.

findings.title: Nav surface is a hard-coded #090a0f band with a dim 8% border, and the sticky blur state is only computed after a scroll event
findings.figma: The Nav frame has no fill (it sits on the page fill #0e1116 = bg/base, mapped --sc-base) and a 1px #2b323d bottom border (= --sc-border). Handoff section 5: sticky on scroll with a subtle bg/base blur + bottom border.
findings.build: Navbar.vue:289-302: position sticky OK, but background is the literal #090a0f (not a token and not --sc-base #0b0d12, so on every page except Home it is a visibly darker band over the page; HomeView.vue:376 hard-codes the same #090a0f for Home only), border-bottom rgba(255,255,255,0.08) = about #1d1e22 (Figma #2b323d), blur(16px) + 0.9 alpha only once scrollY>10. isScrolled is set only by the scroll listener (Navbar.vue:72-74; onMounted :163-168 never calls it), so a reload or hash jump into a scrolled page shows the un-blurred bar until the next scroll.
findings.evidence: dom header bg rgb(9,10,15) vs body background --sc-base rgb(11,13,18); Figma extract 468:126 root.fill null, strokeBottom 1 #2b323d.
findings.fix: background: var(--sc-base); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sc-border); scrolled state color-mix(in srgb, var(--sc-base) 90%, transparent) with the existing blur; call handleScroll() once in onMounted.

findings.title: 44px touch-target floor on nav links, brand and (coarse pointer) CTA exceeds the drawn 17px/39px boxes

findings.build: Navbar.vue:354, :377, :395 .nav-item/.signin-btn/.signout-btn min-height 44px; :330 .brand min-height 44px; :675-677 CTA min-height 44px on coarse pointers only; UiButton.vue:169-173 min-height 44px below 768px and on coarse pointers. The painted desktop sizes are unchanged (the hit area grows, the glyphs do not).

findings.title: 'Active route underline' in handoff section 5 is not drawn in any frame and contradicts section 1
findings.figma: Features/Pricing/Download frames (485:125, 483:125, 487:125) draw the active link as Semi Bold text/primary with no underline or pill. Handoff section 1 says exactly that ('text/primary + Semi Bold').

findings.evidence: Figma scan of the Nav subtree on the three top-nav pages: no stroke/line boxes besides the CTA; MARKETING-SITE-HANDOFF.md section 5 line 'active route underline' vs section 1 line 26-28.
findings.decision: Uma: should the active link also carry an underline? The frames and section 1 say no; section 5 says yes. Recommend: no underline (match the frames) and strike the phrase from section 5.

findings.title: Signed-in nav state is not designed: the code swaps 'Sign in' for 'Account' + 'Sign out'
findings.figma: Only the signed-out nav is drawn, on every frame, including the Account frame 506:124 (its nav 506:125 shows 'Sign in' + 'Download free' even though Account is signed-in only). The Account frame has its own Sign out outline button (506:148, 92x41, r10).
findings.build: Navbar.vue:204-215 (isProbablySignedIn): 'Account' (router-link /account, same muted ink, no active style) and a 'Sign out' <button> (signOut() then router.push('/'), error banner 'We couldn't sign you out...') replace 'Sign in'; the 'Download free' CTA stays. /account therefore shows Sign out twice (nav and the page header).
findings.evidence: account.blink.dom.json (scenario signed-in): signin-btn 'Account' x=1018 and signout-btn 'Sign out' x=1098 in the header; Figma extract of 506:125 texts: Sign in, Download free.
findings.decision: Uma: draw the signed-in nav. Open points: Account link vs avatar/menu, whether Sign out lives in the nav or only on the Account page (it is drawn there at 506:148), whether 'Download free' stays for signed-in users, and the active treatment for Account. Until then the build keeps Account + Sign out.

findings.title: 'Download free' CTA leads to a page where nothing downloads
findings.figma: 'Download free' (468:138, label 14/Bold) is the nav CTA on every page, and the same promise is the primary CTA in the hero (469:131), Pricing, Features and About bands.
findings.build: Navbar.vue:216 (and the mobile sheet :280) route 'Download free' to /download. DownloadView.vue:22-43 and :98-109 state 'No installer is served from this page yet' and render every download button disabled; implementation/api/selahcue_api/apps/downloads and billing contain only __init__/apps/migrations (no models, no endpoints). findings.decision: Owner: keep Figma's 'Download free' (honest /download state already explains the wait), or relabel the CTA (nav, hero, bands) to the honest action until the first signed installer ships? The relabel/removal is owned by 17tnw2b0x3h; this finding only records the nav instance.

Changelog moved to Resources, Blog moved to Resources, 'How it works' added, 'Setup guides' and 'NDI & streaming' absent, Company order differs, Legal is a column with longer labels instead of two short bottom-bar links, and there is no 'Windows · macOS' tag.

findings.title: Footer 'How it works' links to /how-it-works, which has no route and renders the 404 page

The other 12 footer targets (/features /pricing /download /docs /support /blog /changelog /about /careers /contact /affiliates /privacy /terms) all resolve.

findings.figma: Column headings 12/Bold, typed in capitals, +0.1px tracking, #9aa4b2 (muted). Links 14/Regular #eef1f6 (text/primary). Tagline 14/21 #9aa4b2 in a 300px box. findings.title: Footer tagline and legal line carry 'subscription-simple' and 'Cancel anytime', which the repo does not back
findings.figma: Tagline 'Church presentation, done right. Offline-first, subscription-simple, built for the moment that matters.' (479:135, 14/21) and legal line '© 2026 SelahCue · Works offline · Cancel anytime' (479:160), with 'Windows · macOS' on the right.

'Works offline' and 'Windows · macOS' are backed (offline-first invariants, desktop builds for both platforms).

All rights reserved.' value 3.79 (required 4.5, AA-normal) on all 14 public-page captures (about, affiliates, blog, careers, changelog, contact, docs, download, features, home, pricing, privacy, support, terms). Computed: #9aa4b2 on #0e1116 = 7.50.

findings.title: --sc-text-muted (#6b7383) fails AA for small text on every surface it is used on; 40+ consumers
findings.figma: Figma text/muted #9aa4b2: 7.5:1 on #0e1116, 7.2:1 on #14161d, 6.5:1 on #1c1f28 (passes everywhere). The 2.2 mapping sends text/muted to --sc-text-secondary, not --sc-text-muted.
findings.build: tokens.css:13 --sc-text-muted #6b7383 = 4.08:1 on --sc-base, 3.79:1 on --sc-surface, 3.45:1 on --sc-elevated. Consumers beyond the footer and shell: FormField.vue (4 rules), DataTable.vue (4), Toast.vue:102, AdminShell.vue (2), auth.css:110, and 39 sites in views/. The marketing legacy token --text-muted #9aa4b2 (tokens.css:43) passes.
findings.evidence: Computed from the hexes; report.json contrast_survey has 166 entries below 4.5:1 across the run (footer 3.79 on 14 pages, 'Back to Sign in' x10, table headers, '/ month' 4.39 ...). grep -rn 'sc-text-muted' src.
findings.fix: Pick one: (a) re-point small-text uses to var(--sc-text-secondary), which is the documented mapping of text/muted; or (b) raise the token itself so it clears 4.5:1 on --sc-elevated, e.g. #868ea0 (5.0 on elevated, 5.5 on surface, 5.9 on base). Either removes the footer and Loading instances in the same change; page tickets keep their own uses.

findings.title: Gutter and content-width tokens are not what pages use: designed content is 96..1344 (1248 wide), pages render 150..1290 (1140 wide)
findings.figma: Home/Features/Pricing/About section frames: padding 96 left/right at 1440, widest content 1248 at x=96 (Home Features 472:124, Pricing 477:124, Final CTA 479:124, Footer 479:133; hero mock 1140 at x=150 is the one narrower block). Handoff section 3: 96px horizontal gutters.
findings.build: tokens.css:60 --gutter 96px is consumed only by main.css:67-71 .container (used by the footer) and three article views; every public view re-declares .container locally with --page-gutter 24px (tokens.css:64) and its own max-width: Home/About/Features/Support/Contact/Account/Blog 1140, Pricing/Download/Docs 1200, Careers 1000, Navbar 1240, legal 1120. At 1440 that puts content at x=150..1290 instead of 96..1344.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'max-width: 1[0-9][0-9][0-9]px' src/views src/components; dom about cta-card x=150 w=1140; Figma scan: About 496:124 children widest 1248 at x=96.
findings.fix: Define one token (e.g. --content-max: 1248px, gutter 96 at >=1200 / 48 / 20) and one shared .container; page tickets then delete their local max-width/padding overrides. The footer and nav findings above depend on the same token.

findings.title: Section padding token is 100px; Figma sections use 88-90px, and three overlapping section tokens exist
findings.figma: Home sections: Features 88/88, Reliability 90/90, Showcase 90/90, How it works 88/88, Pricing 90/90, Testimonials 90/90, FAQ 90/90, Final CTA 90/90 (frames 472:124 ... 479:124). Handoff section 3: ~88-90px vertical section padding.
findings.build: tokens.css:68 --section-pad: 100px (the one Home, Download and the mobile footer consume: 11 uses), :69 --section-pad-sm: 80px (11 uses), :70 --section-padding: 88px (the right value, consumed only by the unused .section class in main.css:73). --card-radius (16px, :71) and --grid-gap (24px, :73) have no consumers at all.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'var(--section-pad' src: 22 uses of the 100/80 pair, 1 of --section-padding; by padding alone each Home section is 20-24px taller than its Figma frame (100 vs 88-90 top and bottom).
findings.fix: Set --section-pad to 90px (88px sections are within 2px), delete --section-padding, keep one small step for mobile; remove or start consuming --card-radius/--grid-gap (Figma card radii 14-18, grid gaps 20-28).

findings.title: Type-scale tokens match the handoff ramp for Home but nothing consumes them; views hard-code 26-58px headings at weight 800
findings.figma: Handoff section 3 ramp (Inter): H1 60/64 Bold, H2 38-42 Bold, card title 18-21 Semi Bold, body 17-19, small 14-15, eyebrow 13 Bold with tracking. Measured across 14 Figma pages: H1 60/64 (Home) and 46-54 on sub-pages (Features 52/58, Download 52/58, Pricing 52/56, Contact 50/56, Support 48/54, Changelog 48/54, Docs 46/52, Affiliates 54/60); H2 38-42 (Home), 32-40 elsewhere; eyebrow 13/Bold +0.3px; all headings weight 700.
findings.build: tokens.css:51-57: --font-h1 700 60/64, --font-h2 700 42/48, --font-h3 600 21/28, --font-body 400 17/26, --font-small 400 15/22 agree with the ramp, but --font-eyebrow 700 13px/16px has no tracking (a font shorthand cannot carry it) and UiBadge.vue:35 renders eyebrows at 11px. Only BlogPostView.vue:154 uses --font-h1; the .font-h1/.font-h2/.font-h3/.font-body/.font-small/.font-eyebrow classes (main.css:77-82) are unused. Views hard-code: hero H1 58 (Home) / 44 (Features, About) / 40 (Support, Changelog, Blog, Careers) / 48 (Pricing, Download) / 36 (Docs) at font-weight 800; Figma is 700 and 46-54 on sub-pages. (Inter 800 is not even in the Google Fonts request, index.html:11, so 800 renders as the 700 face: visually equal, but every title shows as a weight mismatch.)
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'var(--font-' src: 1 consumer; vp_style_diff on home/features/about shows font-weight figma 700 vs build 800 on every title; Figma aggregate of 14 frames (use_figma text census).
findings.fix: Make the ramp the source: add --font-h1-page (52/58 for sub-page heroes, per the census), give the eyebrow a letter-spacing token (0.3px) and a 13px UiBadge size, set heading weight 700, and let the page tickets replace their local font-size/weight declarations with the tokens.

findings.title: Brand indigo is spelled four ways and the nav hard-codes colours instead of using the token layer
findings.figma: One accent/brand #5b6bd6 across nav CTA, hero, cards and bands; CTA gradient is accent/brand -> #2b2a6b on a 1248x337 r24 CARD (479:125), not on buttons. The 2.2 mapping says to implement accent/brand as --sc-primary.
findings.build: Navbar.vue hard-codes #090a0f, #9aa4b2, #ffffff, #5b6bd6 (:425) and #4f5ec7 (:437) (no var()); tokens.css:81 --gradient-cta starts at #5b6bd6; UiButton primary uses --sc-primary #6e5cf0; Home's CTA band uses #4f46e5 -> #312e81 (HomeView.vue:684). So the nav CTA, the gradient CTAs, the primary buttons and the band are four different indigos on one page.
findings.evidence: dom home: download-cta bg rgb(91,107,214); ui-button variant-primary bg rgb(110,92,240); final-cta-card bgi linear-gradient(135deg, rgb(79,70,229) ..., rgb(49,46,129)); grep -rn 'gradient-cta' src.
findings.fix: Nav CTA and any brand fill: var(--sc-primary); derive --gradient-cta from var(--sc-primary) -> #2b2a6b and use it for the CTA band cards (the page tickets), not for buttons.

findings.title: Button and text colours go through the --sc-* layer (primary #6e5cf0, elevated #1c1f28, border #262a34, text #f4f6fb), a 1-3% luminance gap from Figma's legacy hexes
findings.figma: Figma binds fills to the legacy collection: accent/brand #5b6bd6, bg/elevated #1e232c, border #2b323d, text/primary #eef1f6, text/muted #9aa4b2.
findings.build: UiButton.vue and the shared components use var(--sc-primary) #6e5cf0, var(--sc-elevated) #1c1f28, var(--sc-border) #262a34, var(--sc-text) #f4f6fb, var(--sc-text-secondary) #a7aebe. White on --sc-primary is 4.72:1 (AA), white on Figma's #5b6bd6 is 4.65:1.
findings.evidence: vp_style_diff labels these colour~/fill~ (token layer); computed contrast above.
findings.source: AUTH-LANDING-PAGES-HANDOFF.md section 2.2 (the two token layers: 'Implement with --sc-*').

findings.title: UiButton is a 999px pill everywhere; Figma buttons are 10-12px rounded rectangles, pills only for toggles
findings.figma: Radius measured over every button frame on 15 page frames: 10 (nav CTA 468:138, card actions 'Start guide', 'View role', 'Sign out', 'Manage devices', h39-41), 11 (hero primary 469:131 h49, hero secondary 469:133 h47, pricing card CTAs 477:137/477:166 h44, band buttons h47-49), 12 (sign-in Sign in 505:142 h47 and Google 505:148 h44, affiliates Apply now 541:145 h49). 999 appears only on the Monthly/Annual toggle (483:145, h34) and the hero eyebrow pill (469:125).
findings.build: UiButton.vue:60 border-radius var(--pill-radius) (999px) for every variant and size; auth.css:254-257 already overrides it to 12px for the auth card; the nav CTA is a private 999px pill (Navbar.vue:430).
findings.evidence: dom: ui-button variant-gradient/outline/primary radius '999px' on home, about, features, account, pricing; au-btn radius 12px on signin/reset. vp_style_diff boxes Btn/Download radius figma 10 vs build 999.0.
findings.fix: Default radius by size: sm 10px (h39-41), md/lg 11px (h44-49); keep the 12px au-btn override; keep --pill-radius only for toggles and badges. Remove the auth override's reason to exist by making 12px a UiButton prop if the auth ticket prefers.

findings.title: UiButton height depends on the parent's line-height: the same size renders 41-47 (sm), 47-50.5 (md), 51-58 (lg); Figma uses fixed 39/41/44/47/49
findings.figma: Fixed heights: nav 39 (pad 11/18, 14/Bold), card actions 41 and 39 (pad 12/18, 14/Semi Bold), full-width card CTAs 44 (pad 13/0, 15/Semi Bold), hero and band primary 49 (pad 15/26-28, 15.5/Bold), secondary 47 (pad 14/24, 15.5/Semi Bold).
findings.build: UiButton.vue:85-97: sm 12px 20px / 14px, md 14px 28px / 15px, lg 16px 32px / 16px, weight 600 for all, and no line-height of its own, so height = padding + inherited line box. Measured: lg 58 (Home, About, Features) vs 52 (Contact) vs 51-55 (auth); md 47 (Home/Pricing gradient) vs 50.5 (Support); sm 41-47. Label sizes 14/15/16 vs Figma 14/15/15.5; weight 600 vs Figma 700 on the hero/nav/band primaries.
findings.evidence: dom aggregation of ui-button instances across the 29 captures: 'variant-gradient size-lg' h=58; 'size-lg full-btn' h=52; 'variant-gradient size-md' h=47 vs 50.5; 'variant-outline size-sm' h=43 and 47; Figma scan of all Btn frames (use_figma button census).
findings.fix: Set .ui-button line-height: 1.21 (Inter normal) and re-cut sizes to Figma: sm pad 12px 18px / 14px / h41 (nav compact 11px 18px / 700 / h39), md pad 13px 24px / 15px / h44, lg pad 15px 26px / 15.5px / h49 (secondary lg 14px 24px / h47). Primary lg and nav weight 700, others 600.

findings.title: Variant set does not match Figma: 'gradient' stands in for the solid primary, 'secondary' has no border, and the white/outlined pair for CTA bands does not exist
findings.figma: Figma draws no gradient-filled button (the gradient is the CTA card 479:125, 1248x337 r24). Primary is solid #5b6bd6 (hero 469:131, Get Pro 477:166). Secondary is #1e232c + 1px #2b323d (hero 'Watch 2-min demo' 469:133 with a leading play glyph, pricing 'Download free'/'Talk to us', careers 'View role', sign-in Google). Outline is transparent + 1px #2b323d ('Sign out', 'Manage devices'). On the gradient band: white fill with #5b6bd6 label 15.5/Bold (479:129) and a transparent button with a 1px #ffffff@50% stroke (479:131).
findings.build: UiButton.vue:124-130 gradient variant is used for the hero 'Download free' and Pricing 'Get Pro' (dom home: variant-gradient size-lg/md) where Figma is solid; :108-114 secondary has no border, so pages use 'outline' (transparent) where Figma has the filled secondary (Home hero 'Watch 2-min demo', free-tier card); there is no inverse pair, so HomeView.vue:712-716 forces .cta-btn-white with !important, and About/Features put a gradient button and an outline button on their gradient card.
findings.evidence: dom home: hero Download free 'ui-button variant-gradient size-lg', Watch 2-min demo 'variant-outline size-lg', final CTA 'variant-ghost size-lg cta-btn-white'; about 'variant-gradient size-lg' + 'variant-outline size-lg' inside .cta-card. Figma button census: signatures h49 r11 #fff, h47 r11 stroke #ffffff@0.5, h47 r11 #1e232c + #2b323d.
findings.fix: Make 'primary' the solid CTA (page tickets stop using 'gradient' for buttons), give 'secondary' the 1px var(--sc-border) stroke, keep 'outline', and add 'inverse' (white fill, brand ink, 700) and 'inverse-outline' (1px rgba(255,255,255,.5)) for gradient bands so views stop overriding with !important.

findings.title: UiButton's focus ring is a box-shadow with outline:none, so it disappears in forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) mode
findings.figma: Handoff sections 5 and 6: focus-visible is a 2px accent/brand ring with a 2px offset on every button; Figma draws no focus state.
findings.build: UiButton.vue:66 outline: none and :72-74 box-shadow 0 0 0 2px var(--sc-base), 0 0 0 4px var(--sc-primary). The look matches the spec on screen (2px gap + 2px ring, 4.1:1 against --sc-base, 3.8:1 against --sc-surface), but box-shadow is removed in forced-colors mode, so keyboard users there get no indicator at all (WCAG 2.4.7 / 1.4.11).
findings.evidence: Source read; computed ring contrast #6e5cf0 on #0b0d12 4.12, on #14161d 3.83.
findings.fix: Replace outline:none with outline: 2px solid transparent (a transparent outline is drawn in forced-colors), keep the box-shadow ring for normal mode; or use outline: 2px solid var(--sc-primary); outline-offset: 2px on :focus-visible directly.

findings.title: Hover state is not drawn and the specified direction fails AA: UiButton primary hover is 3.78:1, the nav CTA hover darkens
findings.figma: Frames draw no hover. Handoff section 5: buttons 'hover (lightness shift)' and nav CTA hover 'brand-hover (+8% lightness)'. +8% lightness of #5b6bd6 is about #7c88de, white on it is 3.26:1.
findings.build: UiButton.vue:104-106 primary hover --sc-primary-hover #7e6eff with white 15-16px/600 label = 3.78:1 (resting #6e5cf0 is 4.72:1). Navbar.vue:436-438 nav CTA hover goes DARKER (#4f5ec7, 5.59:1), the opposite direction, so the two primaries behave differently. Gradient hover is a glow (:128-130), secondary/outline/ghost hovers shift to --sc-elevated/--sc-border.
findings.evidence: Computed contrast: white on #7e6eff 3.78, white on #4f5ec7 5.59, white on #7c88de 3.26.
findings.decision: Uma: choose the hover value for primary. A lighter hover cannot hold a white 15px label at 4.5:1 on this indigo; recommend darkening (e.g. the nav's #4f5ec7, 5.59:1) for every primary, and amend section 5 ('+8% lightness') accordingly.

findings.title: Catch-all 404 view renders a second <main> inside the shell's <main>
findings.figma: Not drawn. Handoff section 6 asks for sound semantics (one h1, nav is a <nav>); App.vue:22 provides the page's single <main>, and the captured public pages all have exactly one.
findings.build: NotFoundView.vue:29 <component :is="embedded ? 'div' : 'main'"> renders <main> when not embedded (the catch-all route in router/index.ts:88-92), nested in App.vue's <main class='main-content'>; AdminShell.vue:76 and AffiliateShell.vue:47 (out-of-scope routes) do the same.
findings.evidence: grep -rn '<main' src: App.vue:22, NotFoundView.vue:29 (component :is main), AdminShell.vue:76, AffiliateShell.vue:47; doc.mains is 1 on all 29 captures because no 404 is captured.
findings.fix: NotFoundView: always render a <div class='nf-page'> (drop the :is main branch and the embedded prop's special case), likewise in the two portal shells.

findings.title: Every public page shares one document title
findings.figma: Not drawn (the frames have no browser chrome).
findings.build: index.html:6 sets 'SelahCue — Church presentation, reengineered' and only /privacy, /terms and the article detail pages change it (lib/legal, lib/useDocumentMeta). Home, Features, Pricing, Download, About, Contact, Support, Docs, Changelog, Blog, Careers, Sign in and Account all report the same title, so tabs, history and screen-reader page announcements cannot tell them apart.
findings.evidence: doc.title in each marketing/*.blink.dom.json: identical on about, account, affiliates, blog, careers, changelog, contact, docs, download, features, home, pricing, reset-*, signin, support, verify-*; distinct only on privacy ('SelahCue Privacy Policy') and terms ('SelahCue Terms of Service').
findings.decision: Uma/product: agree the title scheme (e.g. 'Pricing — SelahCue', 'Sign in — SelahCue') and a route meta.title the shell applies on navigation. WCAG 2.4.2 expects a title that describes the page.

findings.title: Route-loading fallback 'Loading...' fails AA (--sc-text-muted on --sc-base, 4.08:1 at 19px)
findings.figma: Handoff section 5 asks for a skeleton/bg-elevated placeholder while content loads; Figma draws no loading text.
findings.build: App.vue:49-56 .loading color var(--sc-text-muted) #6b7383 on --sc-base #0b0d12, 1.2rem (19.2px) at weight 400: 4.08:1, and it is not large text (needs 24px, or 18.66px bold). It is plain text with no status role.
findings.evidence: Computed contrast #6b7383 on #0b0d12 = 4.08; source App.vue:49-56.
findings.fix: .loading color var(--sc-text-secondary) (8.7:1) and add role='status' to the fallback (or render SkeletonLoader).
